coverIntro: Kramer Bouwservice B.V. runs six to seven renovation and small-scale new-build projects at the same time, spread across Noord-Brabant and a bit of Zeeland. This proposal focuses on one concrete problem: during a running project Lisa has no up-to-date margin per project, so course-correcting only happens after the project is already finished.
situation: Every site foreman keeps his own timesheet in a small Excel file and emails it to Lisa every week. Lisa pastes those sheets into a per-project overview by hand and links the purchase invoices - timber, concrete, installation materials - that come in through the accounts by hand as well. That costs her three to four hours every Monday. The result lags by definition: on a project in Bergen op Zoom it only became clear after completion that underestimated material costs had left barely any margin. A month earlier they could still have cut back on extra hours or discussed additional work with the client. An ERP module is not an option: it requires the foremen to type their hours straight into the system, and they are up on the scaffolding, not behind a laptop. The Excel file works for them; the merging on Lisa's end is the problem.
goals: Have an up-to-date margin overview per project every Monday morning before the meeting with Erik, without manual cutting and pasting
Course-correct on margin during a running project instead of finding out afterwards that a project was not profitable
Flag projects that drop below 15% margin early
Free up the three to four hours every Monday now spent on merging for other work
approach: We connect Exact Online - which already holds the purchase invoices and the accounts - to a Power BI dashboard that automatically calculates the margin per project: revenue minus booked hours and purchases. The site foremen keep working the way they are used to; their Excel timesheets remain the source for hours on site. Each foreman emails his own sheet weekly as he does now, and those sheets are read automatically into hours per project, with a normalisation step so that small differences between foremen in columns and project codes are not a problem. Lisa no longer merges anything herself. The dashboard shows the margin per project against one fixed threshold of 15%, and flags projects that drop below it. This way Lisa sees at a glance every Monday morning which projects need attention, before the meeting with Erik starts.
scopeDeliverables: Connection to Exact Online for purchase invoices and accounts per project
Automatic processing of the site foremen's weekly Excel timesheets into hours per project, including a normalisation step for consistent reading
Power BI dashboard with margin per project (revenue minus booked hours and purchases), with one fixed margin threshold of 15%
Alert flag for projects that drop below the threshold
Weekly automatic refresh, ready before the Monday-morning meeting
Short guide for Lisa on submitting the timesheets weekly so the processing keeps working

phases.name: Week 1: scoping and data connection
phases.description: Set up the Exact Online connection for purchases and accounts, align project and cost centre coding, and define the fixed format for the timesheets.

phases.name: Week 2-3: build dashboard
phases.description: Build the Power BI dashboard with margin per project, the fixed 15% threshold, and the alert flag for projects below it.

phases.name: Week 4: test and deliver
phases.description: Run one cycle with real data from running projects, adjust based on feedback from Lisa, and deliver before the next Monday-morning meeting.

investment: This project is scoped as one clearly defined problem - the margin-per-project overview - at a fixed price. We will confirm the exact investment after a short scoping call in which we go through the Exact Online setup, the timesheet format and the desired threshold together.
nextSteps: Approval of this proposal, followed by a short scoping call (about 30 minutes) with Lisa and Erik to go through the Exact Online connection, the timesheet format and the 15% threshold. After that we start straight away in week 1.
